title: 47-foot statue of St. Joseph erected in France after court blocks neighboring nativity scene
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) —In France, installing nativity scenes in public remains a hot topic in the weeks leading up to Christmas. Nevertheless, on November 25, France’s largest nativity scene was set up in the center of Perpignan, a city of over 120,000 inhabitants. It will be officially inaugurated on December 4 and will remain in place until January 10. 👋 #Crèche GÉANTE Mercki @louis_aliot maire @RNational_off de Perpignan pour ce cadeau 👇 https://t.co/Rgkdgnns1g … For Father Benoît de Roeck, rector of Perpignan’s Saint John the Baptist Cathedral and Saint Joseph’s Shrine, the nativity scene in Perpignan is about more than simply preserving a tradition. “A nativity scene reminds us of the significance of this time of year and announces the birth of Christ,” said Father Benoît, noting also that Perpignan’s parishes put up beautiful nativity scenes in their churches. “The initiatives of the city council and the Church coexist and complement one another.” READ: Rioters in France desecrate statues of St. Joan of Arc during violent weekend

title: What Leo XIV gets wrong on the role of husbands and wives
